title: Karakorum becomes a Mongol imperial centre
summary: Karakorum in the Orkhon Valley served as a Mongol imperial centre in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries. Its remains sit within a landscape shaped by pastoral societies and earlier political centres.

claims.text: Karakorum in the Orkhon Valley served as a Mongol imperial centre in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries. Its remains sit within a landscape shaped by pastoral societies and earlier political centres.
Thirteenth–fourteenth-century capital context; no exact foundation year is supplied.

Urban institutions and mobile pastoral lifeways were interconnected. Comparing Karakorum with contemporary cities challenges a simple division between a settled urban world and a separate nomadic one.
